introduction: At this level, we expand our list of crops, understand the specific climatic dependencies of Rabi crops, and look at how seasons blur in Southern India.

core_concepts.title: Expanded Kharif List
core_concepts.description: Alongside Rice and Cotton, remember: Jowar, Bajra (millets require less water but are grown in Kharif), Tur (Arhar), Moong, Urad, and Soyabean.

core_concepts.title: Expanded Rabi List
core_concepts.description: Alongside Wheat and Mustard, remember: Peas, Linseed, Rapeseed, and Coriander.

core_concepts.title: Rabi and Western Disturbances
core_concepts.description: The success of Rabi crops (especially wheat in Punjab and Haryana) is highly dependent on winter rainfall brought by 'Western Disturbances' originating from the Mediterranean Sea.

core_concepts.title: South Indian Exception
core_concepts.description: In Southern India (like Tamil Nadu and Kerala), the temperature remains relatively high year-round. Therefore, there is no distinct winter season. Crops like Rice can be grown continuously all year round if irrigation is available.

important_entities.name: Aus, Aman, and Boro
important_entities.key_fact: Three crops of Rice in a year
important_entities.significance: In states with heavy rainfall and fertile plains like West Bengal and Assam, farmers grow three crops of paddy in a single agricultural year: Aus (Autumn), Aman (Winter/Main), and Boro (Summer).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Millets are dryland crops. Students often think they are Zaid or Rabi because they don't need much water. However, they are primarily grown during the Kharif season in rain-fed areas.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Barley, Mustard, Wheat, Peas. These are all winter (Rabi) crops.

exam_strategy_tips: Questions often ask for the 'odd one out'. For example: Wheat, Barley, Gram, Cotton. (Answer is Cotton, because it's Kharif, the rest are Rabi).
UPSC and State PCS frequently test the 'Aus, Aman, Boro' concept. Remember they are varieties/seasons of RICE.
